title: Security evidence checklist and CISO conversation map
content:
Purpose:
This is a tactical GTM brief for SEs, CSEs and AE technical champions to: 1) quickly assemble evidence for SOC2/ISO/HIPAA conversations; 2) run a concise CISO call mapped to customer risk themes; and 3) provide repeatable, vendor-agnostic audit-log wording and examples that we can commit to in proposals.

Status and intended use:
- Draft guidance: internal use only.
- High priority for mid-market and enterprise demos where security and compliance are gating factors.
- Combine with the full control evidence kit (Confluence INF-AUDIT-42) when responding to RFPs.

High-level positioning (one-liner for SEs):
"Redwood Inference operates with SOC2-aligned controls, extensible audit telemetry, and configurable data residency — enabling secure, auditable LLM inference at scale for regulated workloads."

Conversation map for the first 20 minutes with a CISO or security reviewer:
1) Opening (2–3 min): 
   - Quick intro + context: "we understand you need auditability, tenant separation, and proof of non-exfiltration for PHI/PII".
   - Ask: "Which of these is your priority today: regulatory evidence, runtime telemetry, or contractual commitments?"
2) Risk discovery (5–7 min): 
   - Probe: data types (PHI/PII?), in-transit vs at-rest concerns, retention and deletion SLAs, and vendor access model.
   - Capture: whether they need: HIPAA BAAs, SOC2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert artifacts, or detailed audit-log schema.
3) Technical mapping (7–10 min):
   - Map their ask to Redwood capabilities: private deployment (VPC/on-prem), dedicated isolates, KMS/HSM integrations, per-request audit logs, and model version pinning.
   - Show evidence types available: control narratives, test procedures, sample audit logs, encryption key rotation policy, and retention settings.
4) Close & next steps (1–2 min):
   - Agree on two deliverables: (a) a short evidence packet (SOC2 control narratives + sample logs) and (b) a proposed contractual clause (BPA/BAA or DPA section).

Quick risk-to-feature mapping (for seller talking points):
- Risk: "Vendor can see my inputs" -> Feature: Private deployment / Dedicated capacity / Customer-managed VPC + KMS and BYOK options.
- Risk: "No proof of what happened during inference" -> Feature: Immutable per-request audit logs, cryptographic timestamps, and exportable log bundles.
- Risk: "Regulator asks for retention proof" -> Feature: Configurable retention policies, deletion audit trail, and automated retention reports.

Suggested audit-log wording (language for proposals & SOWs):
- Assertion-style (strong): "Redwood will deliver per-request audit logs containing request id, timestamp (UTC), model id, model version, route, requester id, response hash, and storage retention metadata. Logs will be exportable as JSONL and retained per the agreed retention policy."
- Attestation-style (for pre-sales conversations): "Redwood produces and can deliver audit telemetry that includes API identifiers, timestamps, and model metadata. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers may configure retention and export formats."
- Non-commitment fallback (when legal review pending): "Operational telemetry is available and exportable; specific retention and schema commitments will be finalized in the DPA/SOW."

Recommended minimum audit log schema (example JSON keys – provide to customers as sample):
- request_id: unique UUID per API call
- request_timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- customer_tenant_id: tenant identifier
- model_name: e.g., 'gptx-7b-qa'
- model_hash: truncated model commit/hash (where applicable)
- model_version: pinned version string
- route: api route or endpoint name
- caller_identity: API key id or principal id (obfuscated if needed)
- input_size_tokens: int
- output_size_tokens: int
- response_hash: SHA256(response)
- action_flags: e.g., 'cached', 'served_from_kvcache'
- storage_retention_policy: reference key to agreed retention tier
- deletion_event_id: if deletion occurred, reference to deletion audit entry
- signature: optional cryptographic signature for tamper-evidence

Practices: sample retention tiers to propose:
- short: 7–30 days (default for dev/test)
- standard: 90 days (recommended for most prod workloads)
- long: 1–7 years (regulated/financial/healthcare)
Include: ability to produce a signed "retention proof" stamp on export (time + hash of exported bundle).

HIPAA-specific notes (for BAA discussions):
- Data classification: we treat PHI inputs as sensitive by default. Recommend Private deployment or Dedicated capacity + BAA.
- Minimum evidence requested by healthcare buyers: BAA, SOC2 Type II report, KMS key rotation docs, encryption in transit/at rest verification, and sample audit logs showing access and deletion events.
- Operational guardrails: disable model telemetry sharing in Private deployments; opt-in for hosted inference with explicit customer consent and pseudonymization recommendations.

SOC2 / ISO practicalities (what customers actually want vs what compliance docs say):
- Customers rarely need the raw auditor workpapers; they want control narratives, the latest SOC2 Type II (or attestation letter), and the ability to validate specific controls (e.g., change management, access reviews, incident response).
- For ISO-bound customers: evidence of an ISMS, POA&M, and external certification body report is usually adequate; detailed operational telemetry is a plus.

Competitive notes (quick bullets — what to emphasize vs common competitor gaps):
- Emphasize: unified interface across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so the same audit/logging semantics apply — customers don't have to invent separate observability tools per deployment.
- Competitor gap A: some hosted vendors offer logs but not exportable tamper-evident bundles. Promote our signed export option as differentiator.
- Competitor gap B: several vendors conflate "model telemetry" with customer data access; call out our policy controls and optional model telemetry disable for customers under BAA.
- Competitor gap C: limited route-level or token-level cost/latency tracing. Our token-level cost mapping and per-token latency breakdown can be framed as an operational control for capacity planning and performance SLAs.

Evidence checklist for a short-response RFP (what to attach within 24 hours):
- Redwood: SOC2 Type II cover letter (latest)
- SOC2 control narratives for: access control, change management, encryption, incident response, logging and monitoring
- Sample audit-log export (3 anonymized lines) + schema description
- KMS/HSM integration notes and rotation cadence
- High-level network architecture diagram for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- Proposed DPA excerpts for retention + deletion + audit-log delivery

SE playbook: how to assemble the 24-hr packet
1) Triage: determine if customer needs BAA or SOC2 only.
2) Choose artifact bundle from Confluence folder: {SOC2-latest, control-narratives, sample-logs}.
3) Redact customer-identifying info from sample logs and attach retention tier recommendation.
4) For HIPAA: include BAA template and highlight Private deployment recommendation.
5) Attach a short cover note mapping the artifacts to customer questions.

Common objections and suggested responses:
- "We need immutable logs" -> "We provide signed export bundles with cryptographic hashes; for Private deployments you can bring your own key management for an additional layer of assurance."
- "Can we force-delete data immediately?" -> "Retention deletion is auditable. Immediate purge for hosted offerings can be supported within contractual SLOs; for Dedicated/Private, deletion is under customer control and we provide deletion-event proof."
- "Do you accept annual audits?" -> "Yes — we maintain SOC2 Type II and support customer audits on Dedicated/Private agreements with scoped controls and NDAs in place."

Open questions for legal/compliance to finalize (include in handoff to legal):
- Define exact schema keys we can commit to in the DPA (e.g., will we commit to response_hash?).
- Approve templated retention tiers and deletion SLO language.
- Approve BAA template and whether additional attestation (e.g., HIPAA BA scope) is needed for hosted offerings.

Next steps and owners:
- SEs: use this brief for next five CISO calls this quarter (owner: Maya P.).
- Legal: reconcile proposed audit-log wording with Data Protection team (owner: Priya S.).
- Compliance: prepare an example signed export proof for demo (owner: Jonah K.).

Appendix A — sample short cover note to attach to evidence packet (cut/paste-ready):
"Hi <Name>,
Thanks for the conversation earlier. Per our discussion, attached is a short evidence packet that maps to the controls you asked about (SOC2 control narratives, sample anonymized audit log, KMS notes, and BAA template). If you'd like a deeper dive into any control or a scoped audit on Dedicated/Private, we can schedule a walkthrough with our Compliance team.
Regards,
<Maya Patel>"

Appendix B — one-line callouts for slide decks (snappy bullets):
- "SOC2 Type II + exportable tamper-evident audit logs"
- "Private/Dedicated deployments for PHI use cases + BAA"
- "Retention & deletion proof for compliance evidence"

End of doc.
